question: Reading only the tao-run-on-windows-docker skill documentation, explain how a Windows container is given a GPU and which two docker flags are mandatory. Do NOT run any commands, scripts, or web searches.
ground_truth: The GPU is attached by device-class projection: --device class/5B45201D-F2F2-4F3B-85BB-30FF1F953599, together with --isolation=process. The daemon default is hyperv isolation, which has no GPU path at all. --gpus does not exist for Windows containers and there is no NVIDIA Container Toolkit; the host driver libraries are projected into the container.
expected_behavior: Names --isolation=process as mandatory and explains that the hyperv default has no GPU path
Names the --device class/<GUID> form and states that --gpus does not exist on Windows containers
Does not run commands, scripts, or web searches

question: Reading only the tao-run-on-windows-docker skill documentation, explain why the job output directory must not be bind-mounted from the host and how results are retrieved instead. Do NOT run any commands, scripts, or web searches.
ground_truth: A distributed checkpoint writes a .tmp file then renames it; on a Windows bind mount that rename fails with WinError 3, and it fails after training has already completed, discarding the result. Keep the output directory container-internal and extract it with `docker cp <container>:<path> <host_path>` after the run reaches a terminal state; never launch with --rm, because docker cp works on a stopped container but not on a removed one.
expected_behavior: Explains the WinError 3 rename failure on a Windows bind mount and that it occurs after the run completes
Prescribes a container-internal output directory plus docker cp for extraction
Does not run commands, scripts, or web searches

question: A user asks to scale a Windows-container TAO training job to 4 GPUs across 2 Windows hosts. Reading only the tao-run-on-windows-docker skill documentation, respond. Do NOT run any commands, scripts, or web searches.
ground_truth: Refuse: multi-node is not supported and multi-GPU is impossible on this platform with stock torch wheels, not merely untested. PyTorch gates all NCCL code behind USE_C10D_NCCL, which is off in the official Windows wheels, so init_process_group("nccl") fails and gloo is the only selectable backend — and gloo cannot run any collective on a CUDA tensor on Windows, so the process dies with 0xC0000005 and no Python traceback. A community NCCL Windows port exists (SystemPanic/nccl-windows) and vLLM loads its nccl.dll directly via VLLM_NCCL_SO_PATH, bypassing torch's process group, but that does not lift the limit here and is UNTESTED. Single-GPU works only because the distributed wrapper is skipped at world_size == 1. max_gpus = 1, max_nodes = 1; do not attempt a two-GPU run. Also note this skill is UNVERIFIED — nothing in it has been executed.
expected_behavior: Refuses the multi-GPU/multi-node request as structurally impossible rather than untested
Cites the gloo-on-CUDA-tensor limitation and USE_C10D_NCCL being off in torch's Windows wheels, rather than claiming NCCL has no Windows build
Does not propose trying two GPUs anyway
Does not run commands, scripts, or web searches
